sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Let me check what each palette color paints
# First clear
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 60, 'col': 34}])
for r in range(3):
    for c in range(3):
        row = 28 + r * 6 + 3
        col = 38 + c * 6 + 3
        action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': row, 'col': col}])

# Palette positions (row 60, cols 34, 40, 46, 52, 58, 64, 70, 76, 82)
# Colors: black, blue, yellow, green, gray, magenta, orange, sky blue, dark red
palette_colors = ['black', 'blue', 'yellow', 'green', 'gray', 'magenta', 'orange', 'sky_blue', 'dark_red']
palette_cols = [34, 40, 46, 52, 58, 64, 70, 76, 82]

# Test each color by painting (0, 0) and checking the result
paint_results = {}
for i, (color, col) in enumerate(zip(palette_colors, palette_cols)):
    if color == 'black':
        continue  # Skip black (clear)
    # Select color
    action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 60, 'col': col}])
    # Paint (0, 0)
    action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 30, 'col': 40}])
    # Check what color was painted
    seg = current_frame.segmentation
    painted_color = None
    for n in seg['nodes']:
        b = n['boundary']
        rmin = min(p[0] for p in b)
        cmin = min(p[1] for p in b)
        if rmin == 28 and cmin == 38:  # (0, 0) cell
            painted_color = n['color']
            break
    paint_results[color] = painted_color
    # Clear (0, 0) for next test
    action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 60, 'col': 34}])
    action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 30, 'col': 40}])

print("Paint results:")
for color, result in paint_results.items():
    print(f"  {color} -> {result}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
